title: Cricovo
summary: A cricket tournament management platform - live scorecards, stats, and a full organizer toolkit for local and regional tournaments.
description: Cricovo is a cricket tournament management platform - part live-scores site, part organizer toolkit. Anyone can follow a tournament without an account; organizers, team owners, and players get full tools to run one end-to-end, from team approvals and fixtures to ball-by-ball scorecards and auto-computed stats. Think of it as a lightweight Cricbuzz for local and regional tournaments, with the admin tooling built right in.
highlights: Full ball-by-ball scorecards - batting, bowling, extras, fall of wickets, and Player of the Match
Auto-computed points tables and cross-tournament player career stats, always up to date
Role-based access for public visitors, players, team owners, and organizers with Google Sign-In
Kept warm on Render via a scheduled GitHub Actions health-check

title: DrawHunt
summary: A real-time multiplayer draw-and-guess game - one player sketches the secret word on a shared canvas while everyone else races to guess it in live chat.
description: DrawHunt is a fast-paced, real-time multiplayer draw-and-guess game built on Flask and Flask-SocketIO. One player draws a chosen secret word on a shared canvas while everyone else races against the clock to crack it in live chat. Stroke data streams as lightweight vector segments rather than images, correct guesses are intercepted server-side so the word never leaks, and stable client identities let players survive refreshes mid-game.
highlights: Low-latency vector canvas - stroke data streamed as segments per frame, not images
Server-side guess detection keeps the secret word from ever leaking to other players
Stable client identities survive page refreshes, with host migration if the creator drops
Dynamic letter hints, time-based scoring, and an animated podium finish

title: Super Cards
summary: A real-time multiplayer card-game platform - Super Seven, Super Four, and Bluff, all sharing one lobby, room system, and live gameplay engine.
description: Super Cards is a real-time multiplayer card-game platform built with Flask-SocketIO and vanilla JavaScript. Players create a room, pick a game, invite friends, and jump into a shared table directly in the browser. It has grown beyond a single game into a home for multiple card experiences under one consistent lobby, room system, and live gameplay flow - Super Seven's tactical shedding, Super Four's hidden-card memory play, and Bluff's deception and challenge mechanics.
highlights: Three games (Super Seven, Super Four, Bluff) sharing one room and lobby platform
Server-authoritative rules, timers, and turn flow for fair play
Custom-generated SVG card art instead of third-party assets
Reconnection and host hand-off keep live sessions stable

title: Cricket Analysis & Prediction
summary: A Flask app that predicts IPL first-innings scores from live match state, backed by historical team, venue, and player stats.
description: A Flask web app that analyses IPL match data and predicts first-innings scores using a linear regression model trained on IPL 2008-2016 data. Beyond the score predictor, it surfaces historical win/loss records by team, a toss advisor for bat-or-field decisions by venue, average first-innings scores across venues, and career stats for any IPL player.
highlights: Live score predictor from match state - teams, venue, overs, runs, wickets
Toss Advisor - bat-or-field recommendation from historical venue win rates
Career stats lookup for any IPL player, plus venue and team-level historicals

title: Line Encoder & Scrambler
summary: Seven classic digital line-encoding schemes and two scrambling techniques, implemented from scratch in Python with a visual preview.
description: An implementation of classic digital line-encoding schemes - NRZ-L, NRZ-I, RZ, Manchester, Differential Manchester, AMI, and pseudoternary - plus the advanced scrambling techniques B8ZS and 4B5B, built from first principles rather than a signal-processing library.
highlights: Seven line-encoding schemes: NRZ-L, NRZ-I, RZ, Manchester, Differential Manchester, AMI, pseudoternary
B8ZS and 4B5B scrambling for AMI and high-density encoding

title: OCR String Similarity
summary: A visually-grounded weighted Levenshtein distance for OCR error correction - built from actual glyph similarity, not arbitrary substitution costs.
description: Standard Levenshtein treats every substitution equally - replacing O with 0 costs the same as replacing O with X. But OCR errors aren't random; they happen because characters look alike. This library renders each character as a glyph across multiple fonts, measures perceptual distance between every pair with SSIM (structural similarity), and builds a substitution-cost matrix so visually similar pairs get a lower edit cost - the same class of problem behind production OCR parser work at Perfios.
highlights: Substitution costs derived from SSIM glyph similarity across multiple fonts, not guesswork
O(1) substitution lookup at runtime via a precomputed, cached matrix
Applies to post-OCR fuzzy matching, confidence scoring, and document-digitisation pipelines

title: Salary Predictions
summary: A regression model that predicts software-developer salaries from experience and skills.
description: A machine-learning project that predicts software-developer salaries from features like experience and skill set, wrapped in a simple, explainable regression model.
highlights: Salary prediction via regression
Feature engineering on developer attributes

title: PDF Processing Toolkit
summary: A collection of PDF-processing experiments — text extraction, layout analysis, and structure parsing from complex documents.
description: Jupyter notebooks exploring PDF text extraction, table detection, and layout parsing techniques — the same class of problems behind my day-job data-mining pipelines.
highlights: Text extraction and structure parsing from complex PDFs
Table detection and layout analysis experiments
